scenarios.caption: Owned at hyperscaler volume. Compute is charged on every provisioned GPU-hour at $1.50; the model lab takes 30% of revenue as a license fee; the operator keeps $16.5B, or $3.95 per chip-hour.

Rented at $3.00 per chip-hour. Revenue and license fee are unchanged; compute expense doubles to $12.6B and profit falls to $10.3B, or $2.45 per chip-hour. The rented fleet breaks even at 33% utilization; the owned fleet at 16.5%.

summary: InferenceX AgentX measures how many agentic-coding tokens a production serving stack delivers at a fixed interactivity target. Priced at Kimi K3's public OpenRouter rates and scaled to one gigawatt of provisioned power, the MI355X vLLM result is $32.6 billion of revenue per year at P90 45 tok/s/user and 60% utilization.
callout: Owned at hyperscaler volume ($1.50 per chip-hour), the fleet keeps $16.5 billion of profit at a 50.7% margin. Rented on a 3-year contract at August 2026 pricing ($3.00 per chip-hour), it keeps $10.3 billion at 31.5%.
method: 6,115 tok/s per GPU at P90 45 tok/s/user, interpolated on the measured MI355X vLLM frontier (FP4, MTP, TP8).
478,469 GPUs per gigawatt at 2.09 kW all-in per chip; 60% of benchmarked throughput is sold.
$0.59 per million tokens blended: 99.2% of tokens are input and 93.7% of those hit the prefix cache.
Profit = revenue − compute (every GPU-hour, busy or idle) − 30% model license fee.
footnote: Figures are estimates from benchmark throughput and public list prices, not forecasts of any operator's results.
